ref_extractions.title: Separating Phonological and Semantic Processing in Auditory Sentence Processing: A High-Resolution Event-Related Brain Potential Study
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper investigates PMN and N400 components during auditory sentence processing with phonological and semantic manipulations. It studies language processing in a different modality (auditory sentence matching) and uses a completely different experimental paradigm unrelated to VR environments or the RAND/REF × DARK/LIGHT design.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Separate auditory sentence ERP study examining phonological mismatch negativity (PMN) and N400 during speech perception; no connection to VR EEG dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Brain Potentials Distinguish New and Studied Objects During Working Memory
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses delayed match-to-sample tasks with common visual objects to examine working memory processes and old-new ERP effects. The paradigm and research questions are fundamentally different from VR-based visual prediction-error ERP responses, and no reference to the VR dataset or RAND/REF stimulus conditions exists.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Working memory study with delayed match-to-sample paradigm measuring P3 and old-new effects for visual objects; unrelated experimental design and dataset.

ref_extractions.title: How Does Arabic Orthographic Connectivity Modulate Brain Activity During Visual Word Recognition: An ERP Study
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper investigates N170 component modulation by Arabic orthographic connectivity during lexical decision tasks on connected/non-connected word types. The study focuses on reading processes and language expertise, which is entirely unrelated to VR prediction-error paradigms or the RAND/REF × DARK/LIGHT event structure of the target dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Arabic visual word recognition study using lexical decision tasks; examines N170 responses to orthographic connectivity; no VR component or prediction-error paradigm.

ref_extractions.title: Towards OPM-MEG in a virtual reality environment
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper focuses on OPM-MEG (optically-pumped magnetoencephalography) technology, not EEG. While it discusses VR environments and wearable neuroimaging, it does not use the openneuro_ds005841 EEG dataset. The paper demonstrates novel MEG hardware in VR rather than analyzing ERP responses to visual stimuli.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: MEG modality, different technology; VR context but not using this dataset

ref_extractions.title: Virtual body ownership affects the processing of sensorimotor contingencies and goal-oriented information extraction, but not semantics
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses EEG in VR and studies ERP components (N2, P3b, N400) related to breaks in presence. However, the dataset is from their own study hosted on OSF (osf.io/s9hyk) and GitHub (ucc-general/PresenceEEGFollowup), not the openneuro_ds005841 dataset. Different experimental paradigm (slingshot game with embodied BIPs).
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Uses own OSF/GitHub dataset; different VR paradigm (embodiment slingshot game)

ref_extractions.title: Right Hemisphere Sensitivity to Word- and Sentence-Level Context: Evidence From Event-Related Brain Potentials
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper studies language comprehension and hemispheric asymmetry using laterally presented word pairs in sentences. It measures ERPs but is focused on psycholinguistic questions about word/sentence context, not VR stimulus classification. Does not use openneuro_ds005841 or any VR paradigm.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Language/psycholinguistics ERPs; no VR component; no relation to this dataset

ref_extractions.title: Evaluating Models of Object-Decision Priming: Evidence From Event-Related Potential Repetition Effects
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper studies ERP repetition effects in object-decision priming using line drawings of possible/impossible 3D objects. It has no connection to VR environments, the lighting/reference paradigm, or the specific OpenNeuro dataset ds005841.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: ERP study on priming with line drawings; different paradigm and stimuli, no VR component, no dataset reference

ref_extractions.title: Processing of visual semantic information to concrete words: temporal dynamics and neural mechanisms indicated by event-related brain potentials
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper investigates ERPs during object working memory tasks with auditory word stimuli (concrete vs abstract words). It does not use VR stimuli, the 2x2 lighting/reference design, or the OpenNeuro VR dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: ERP study on semantic processing of words; uses polygons and lexical decision tasks, completely different paradigm from VR visual ERP study

ref_extractions.title: Does facilitation by phonological cuing in picture naming depend on the modality of the cue?
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper examines phonological cuing effects on picture naming in healthy and aphasic participants using auditory, visual, and audiovisual cues. It does not involve VR environments, prediction-error paradigms, or the specific dataset ds005841.

ref_extractions.title: The time course of orthography and phonology: ERP correlates of masked priming effects in Spanish
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper examines ERP correlates of masked priming in visual word recognition using Spanish lexical decision tasks. It has no connection to the openneuro_ds005841 VR experiment or its stimulus classification paradigm.

ref_extractions.title: Neurophysiological evidence for the influence of past experience on figure-ground perception
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper investigates how past experience influences early shape assignment using ERPs while participants view silhouettes. While it involves ERPs and visual perception, it does not use or reference the openneuro_ds005841 dataset, which involves VR-based visual stimulus classification with orthogonal lighting/reference dimensions.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: ERP study on figure-ground perception and shape familiarity, unrelated to VR stimulus classification dataset

ref_extractions.title: Comparison of tactile, auditory, and visual modality for brain-computer interface use: a case study with a patient in the locked-in state
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper is a case study with a locked-in patient comparing BCI modalities (tactile, auditory, visual) using oddball paradigms for communication. While it involves EEG/ERP, it is completely unrelated to VR environments, the openneuro_ds005841 dataset's 2x2 lighting/reference design, or any VR stimulus classification task.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: BCI study with LIS patient using oddball paradigms; different domain entirely from VR-EEG classification

ref_extractions.title: ERP correlates of word production predictors in picture naming: a trial by trial multiple regression analysis from stimulus onset to response
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper investigates ERP correlates during picture naming tasks with 31 participants, analyzing psycholinguistic variables (Age of Acquisition, Name Agreement, etc.) on word production latencies. This is a language production study with overt naming, completely unrelated to the VR-based visual stimulus classification task in openneuro_ds005841.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Picture naming language study; different paradigm, stimulus type, and cognitive domain from VR visual classification

ref_extractions.title: Haptic, Virtual Interaction and Motor Imagery: Entertainment Tools and Psychophysiological Testing
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper describes a general VR/affordance study with 10 subjects using Leap Motion for motor imagery training with ERPs. It discusses VR and EEG methodology but does not reference or use the openneuro_ds005841 dataset, which is a separate VR-ERP study with 48 subjects using a 2x2 lighting/reference paradigm.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Paper describes a different study with different setup (Leap Motion, 10 subjects, affordance recognition task) than dataset ds005841 (48 subjects, 73 channels, VR lighting/reference paradigm with RAND_DARK/LIGHT and REF_DARK/LIGHT events). No dataset reference found.

ref_extractions.title: Validation of the Emotiv EPOC EEG gaming system for measuring research quality auditory ERPs
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper is a validation study comparing Emotiv EPOC commercial EEG headset against Neuroscan research EEG for auditory ERP measurement (standard/deviant tones). It has nothing to do with VR environments or the openneuro_ds005841 dataset's visual stimulus classification paradigm.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Paper focuses on validating a consumer EEG device for auditory ERPs with 21 subjects and tone stimuli. Does not mention VR, lighting conditions, or the specific openneuro_ds005841 dataset. Paradigm is entirely different (auditory vs visual VR).

feasibility_reason: The dataset has an exceptionally well-defined event structure (4 balanced event classes with 288 trials each) and a clear VR stimulus classification task described in analysis.md. While no reference papers are 'relevant' or 'partial', the dataset is hosted on OpenNeuro (a well-known public repository) with detailed paradigm documentation, meeting the exception criteria. The 2x2 factorial design (lighting × reference type) provides clear classification targets for EEG-based decoding.

## Tasks

### Potential Task 1: VR Visual Stimulus Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s, target_events = [`event_1`, `event_2`, `event_3`, `event_4`, `event_5`, `event_6`, `event_7`, `event_8`, `event_11`, `event_12`, `event_13`, `event_14`, `event_15`, `event_16`, `event_17`, `event_18`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `event_1` | 0 | Stimulus event (condition group 1) |
  | `event_2` | 1 | Stimulus event (condition group 2) |
  | `event_3` | 2 | Stimulus event (condition group 3) |
  | `event_4` | 3 | Stimulus event (condition group 4) |
  | `event_5` | 4 | Stimulus event (condition group 5) |
  | `event_6` | 5 | Stimulus event (condition group 6) |
  | `event_7` | 6 | Stimulus event (condition group 7) |
  | `event_8` | 7 | Stimulus event (condition group 8) |
  | `event_11` | 8 | Stimulus event (condition group 9) |
  | `event_12` | 9 | Stimulus event (condition group 10) |
  | `event_13` | 10 | Stimulus event (condition group 11) |
  | `event_14` | 11 | Stimulus event (condition group 12) |
  | `event_15` | 12 | Stimulus event (condition group 13) |
  | `event_16` | 13 | Stimulus event (condition group 14) |
  | `event_17` | 14 | Stimulus event (condition group 15) |
  | `event_18` | 15 | Stimulus event (condition group 16) |
- **Kernel Notes**: Verify event-to-condition mapping via companion file before finalizing labels. Paradigm describes a 2×2 design (lighting: DARK/LIGHT × predictability: RAND/REF) yielding 4 conditions, but actual event IDs (event_1 through event_18) differ from paradigm labels. Apply bandpass filter (1–40 Hz) to attenuate VR motion artifacts. Use ICA for artifact removal prior to epoching. Baseline correction using pre-stimulus interval (-0.2 to 0 s). Expect ~1400 trials per event class across 288 files. Primary contrasts for 4-condition analysis: RAND vs REF (prediction error) and DARK vs LIGHT (luminance).

### Potential Task 2: VR Prediction Error Response (RAND vs REF)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s, target_events = [`event_1`, `event_2`, `event_3`, `event_4`, `event_5`, `event_6`, `event_7`, `event_8`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `event_1` | 0 | Random/predictable stimulus (group A) |
  | `event_2` | 0 | Random/predictable stimulus (group A) |
  | `event_3` | 0 | Random/predictable stimulus (group A) |
  | `event_4` | 0 | Random/predictable stimulus (group A) |
  | `event_5` | 1 | Random/predictable stimulus (group B) |
  | `event_6` | 1 | Random/predictable stimulus (group B) |
  | `event_7` | 1 | Random/predictable stimulus (group B) |
  | `event_8` | 1 | Random/predictable stimulus (group B) |
- **Kernel Notes**: Binary classification for prediction error analysis. After verifying condition mapping via companion file, collapse events into RAND vs REF groups. Focus on N200/P300 components sensitive to predictability. VR motion artifacts likely; ensure ICA-based artifact removal.

### Potential Task 3: VR Luminance Response (DARK vs LIGHT)
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s, target_events = [`event_11`, `event_12`, `event_13`, `event_14`, `event_15`, `event_16`, `event_17`, `event_18`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `event_11` | 0 | Dark/light stimulus (group A) |
  | `event_12` | 0 | Dark/light stimulus (group A) |
  | `event_13` | 0 | Dark/light stimulus (group A) |
  | `event_14` | 0 | Dark/light stimulus (group A) |
  | `event_15` | 1 | Dark/light stimulus (group B) |
  | `event_16` | 1 | Dark/light stimulus (group B) |
  | `event_17` | 1 | Dark/light stimulus (group B) |
  | `event_18` | 1 | Dark/light stimulus (group B) |
- **Kernel Notes**: Binary classification for luminance effect analysis. Expected to show amplitude differences in early visual components (P100, N100) due to different lighting conditions in VR. Apply bandpass filter (1–40 Hz) and ICA artifact removal before epoching.

### Potential Task 4: Mismatched Negativity / Prediction Error Mismatch Analysis
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 0.6 s, target_events = [`event_1`, `event_2`, `event_3`, `event_4`, `event_5`, `event_6`, `event_7`, `event_8`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `event_1` | 0 | Standard/predictable visual stimulus |
  | `event_2` | 0 | Standard/predictable visual stimulus |
  | `event_3` | 0 | Standard/predictable visual stimulus |
  | `event_4` | 0 | Standard/predictable visual stimulus |
  | `event_5` | 1 | Deviant/unpredictable visual stimulus |
  | `event_6` | 1 | Deviant/unpredictable visual stimulus |
  | `event_7` | 1 | Deviant/unpredictable visual stimulus |
  | `event_8` | 1 | Deviant/unpredictable visual stimulus |
- **Kernel Notes**: Analysis of prediction error responses via mismatched negativity-like components. Collapsed across luminance conditions to focus on predictability dimension. Expected to show enhanced N200/P300 for unpredictable (RAND) vs predictable (REF) stimuli. Verify condition assignment via companion file. ICA recommended for VR artifact removal.

### Potential Task 5: Visual ERP Component Analysis
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 0.5 s, target_events = [`event_53`, `event_55`, `event_56`, `event_57`, `event_58`, `event_59`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `event_53` | 0 | Visual stimulus event (subset A) |
  | `event_55` | 1 | Visual stimulus event (subset B) |
  | `event_56` | 2 | Visual stimulus event (subset C) |
  | `event_57` | 3 | Visual stimulus event (subset D) |
  | `event_58` | 4 | Visual stimulus event (subset E) |
  | `event_59` | 5 | Visual stimulus event (subset F) |
- **Kernel Notes**: Small-count events (41–48 trials) may represent rare/target stimuli or response events. Analysis window tmax=0.5s optimized for early visual ERP components (P100, N100). Apply bandpass filter (1–40 Hz). Low trial count suggests single-trial classification or averaging across subjects for reliable component extraction.

### Potential Task 6: Event-Related Response Detection
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 1.0 s, target_events = [`event_65536`, `event_65548`]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: raw
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `event_65536` | 0 | Special event type (2 trials) |
  | `event_65548` | 1 | Special event type (3 trials) |
- **Kernel Notes**: Very rare events (2–3 trials) likely represent unique markers or system events. Due to extremely low trial count, recommend excluding from standard classification or pooling across subjects for event detection analysis only. May indicate start/end markers or system synchronization pulses.
